title: Three Gateways, One Quota
description: Three gateways each maintain a local 100/minute tenant counter. One tenant spreads requests across gateways and gets 300/minute. What enforces one quota within this region?

options.text: Keep local counters and return 429 more descriptively.
options.explanation: A better response message does not coordinate the three independent budgets.

options.text: Read a shared counter and decrement in a separate call.
options.explanation: Concurrent requests can pass the same check before either decrement. The decision must be atomic.

options.text: Use source IP instead of tenant identity.
options.explanation: IP changes the policy and can punish NAT users or be bypassed; it does not enforce the authenticated tenant's quota.

options.text: Use shared tenant state with atomic check-and-update, and define the store's failure policy.
options.explanation: A Redis script can combine refill and decrement without races. Shared state adds a dependency; strict multi-region limits need further budget or authority design.
